latest_release.name: v0.2.0
latest_release.body:
## 🌞 SO3LR v0.2.0 Release Notes

This release introduces the SO3LR Tauri models, the flash MD engine with multi-GPU support, the SO3krates code inside the repository for training and fine-tuning, and many other features and fixes (see below). Extended docs moved to [so3lr.github.io](https://so3lr.github.io/).

### New Features
- **SO3LR Tauri models** (`so3lr-tauri-s`, `-m`, `-l`) covering H to At (Z = 1–85). `so3lr-tauri-m` is the new default, `-l` is the most accurate (recommended for reactions), and `-s` is the fastest. Each model also has a dated name (for example `so3lr-tauri-m-2606`) that always refers to the same weights; the earlier `-2602` models are the checkpoints after stage 4 of training (see the [preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2611.06237)). The original model stays available as `so3lr`.
- **Flash MD engine** with fused GPU kernels (JAX Pallas, plus CUDA kernels on NVIDIA GPUs). It gives the same energies and forces as the neighbour-list potential, and it is the default MD engine wherever it applies (`--engine auto`). On an A100 with `so3lr-tauri-m`, flash is 3.7–4.0× faster than the neighbour-list engine with the Pallas kernels and about 9–10× faster with the CUDA kernels. The flash engine also lowers the peak memory per atom by 140–480× and allows up to 9 million atoms on an A100 (40 GB) and 84 million atoms on an AMD MI355X (288 GB).
- **Multiple GPUs and large systems**: `--flash-devices N` enables parallelization across several GPUs of one node (4 A100s run 3.2–4.0× faster than one). `FlashDomains` evaluates a system in chunks (domains), which allows up to 384 million atoms on an A100 (40 GB) and 2.04 billion atoms on an MI355X (288 GB), with real-space long range only (no PME).
- **Guided terminal interface**: `so3lr start` sets up MD, optimization or evaluation step by step, and runs show live plots. `so3lr show` monitors running and finished runs (`--json` for scripts), and `so3lr resume` continues a run from its last checkpoint.
- **One precision flag**, `--precision float32|mixed|float64`, for MD, `opt`, `eval` and `tune-ewald` and in the Python calculators. `mixed` runs a float32 model around a float64 MD state.
- **Long-range and evaluation upgrades**: P3M electrostatics, k-space dispersion, k-space in `so3lr eval` for periodic datasets, embeddings and per-atom observables from `eval`, and `tune-ewald` on the flash engine for systems of tens of thousands of atoms.
- **`So3lrEngine`** to drive SO3LR from other MD codes (OpenMM, i-PI, LAMMPS or your own loop), and **`FlashCalculator`** for ASE on the flash engine.
- **Enhanced sampling with PySAGES**: ABF, spectral ABF, well-tempered metadynamics and harmonic biasing. Collective variables include proton-transfer CVs, and a cylindrical restraint is available for host-guest binding.
- **Training from scratch** with `so3lr train`: EMA of weights, early stopping, learning-rate reduction on plateau, k-space during training, and data-parallel training on all local GPUs.
- **Fine-tuning that keeps the long-range terms intact** on data with only energies and forces, with three [recipes](https://so3lr.github.io/training/finetuning/#choosing-a-strategy): anchors to the starting model (`training.long_range_anchor_weights`), an exact long range with `--strategy readout_only` and a residual energy readout (`model.energy_residual_mlp_widths`), or pseudo-labels from a teacher model. Periodic data can be fine-tuned with k-space (`model.cutoff_lr`, `model.kspace_electrostatics`).
- **SO3krates (mlff) is now part of the repository** (`so3lr/mlff`): refactored SO3krates code (from 21.6k to 12.6k lines) based on the [`mlff`](https://github.com/kabylda/mlff/tree/v1.0_dev_import) package. The model, data loading and training code no longer come from a separate install, so models, training and MD are versioned together.
- **More MD options**: Langevin thermostat (`nvt-langevin`), semi-isotropic NPT (experimental), frozen atoms (`fixed_atom_indices` /

![workflow-test-ci](https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/actions/workflows/CI.yml/badge.svg) [![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-so3lr.github.io-4a9d4a)](https://so3lr.github.io/) [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/blob/main/examples/so3lr_colab_example.ipynb) [![cite-link](https://img.shields.io/badge/how_to-cite-000000)](#citation) [![preprint-link](https://img.shields.io/badge/preprint-arXiv-B31B1B)](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2611.06237) [![paper-link](https://img.shields.io/badge/paper-JACS-FFCE34)](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c09558) [![data](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.22920714.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22920714)

## About SO3LR - pronounced *Solar* - is a pretrained machine-learned force field for (bio)molecular simulations. It integrates the fast and stable SO3krates neural network for semi-local interactions with universal pairwise force fields designed for short-range repulsion, long-range electrostatics, and dispersion interactions. ## Installation Try SO3LR without any local installation using our [light web version](https://so3lr.github.io/gui/) or [Colab notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/github/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/blob/main/examples/so3lr_colab_example.ipynb). We recommend installing SO3LR with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (it's magical): ```shell git clone https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr.git cd so3lr uv sync --locked --extra cuda12 # GPU; drop --extra cuda12 for CPU source .venv/bin/activate so3lr --help ``` If JAX is already installed on your cluster (CUDA or ROCm), install SO3LR into that environment: ```shell git clone https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr.git cd so3lr uv pip install ".[cuda12]" # NVIDIA GPU; ROCm or CPU: uv pip install . so3lr --help ``` See the [installation guide](https://so3lr.github.io/installation/) for optional extras. More details about JAX installation can be found [here](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/installation.html). ## Quick start SO3LR provides a command-line interface for geometry optimization, molecular dynamics and evaluation. Each command can be run with `--help` to see all available options. ```shell # Geometry optimization so3lr opt --input geometry.xyz --force-conv 0.05 # NVT and NPT molecular dynamics so3lr nvt --input geometry.xyz --temperature 300 --dt 0.5 --md-cycles 100 --md-steps 100 so3lr npt --input geometry.xyz --temperature 300 --pressure 1.0 --dt 0.5 --md-cycles 100 --md-steps 100 # Evaluation on a dataset so3lr eval --datafile dataset.extxyz --lr-cutoff 100 --save-to predictions.extxyz ``` For longer simulations, use a settings file, `so3lr --settings settings.yaml` (see [molecular dynamics](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/md/)). To use SO3LR as an ASE calculator: ```python from ase.io import read from so3lr import So3lrCalculator atoms = read("geometry.xyz") atoms.info["charge"] = 0 # total charge; 0 if unset atoms.calc = So3lrCalculator(model="so3lr-tauri-m", lr_cutoff=100) energy = atoms.get_potential_energy() forces = atoms.get_forces() ``` Units are eV and Å. On the command line, periodic structures use PME for electrostatics and dispersion with a 10 Å real-space cutoff (2 Å smearing, 1.55 Å mesh), as in the paper's liquid and scaling simulations. The original `so3lr` model keeps real space up to 12 Å, as in v0.1.0. The Python calculators default to 12 Å without k-space. For gas-phase simulations, we suggest using `--lr-cutoff 100`. ## Models The models are bundled with the package and selected by name. The SO3LR Tauri models cover H to At (Z = 1–85) and are described in the [SO3LR Tauri preprint](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2611.06237). - `so3lr-tauri-m` (default): start here; the model we use for biomolecular MD. - `so3lr-tauri-l`: the most accurate, recommended for reactions; 3.7× slower than `-m`. - `so3lr-tauri-s`: 1.4× faster than `-m`. - `so3lr`: the original model from the [JACS paper](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c09558), for H, C, N, O, F, P, S and Cl, kept to reproduce published results. Use the same name on the command line (`--model`) and in settings files (`model:`), or pass a path to a fine-tuned model. To pin a release for papers and benchmarks, add its date: `so3lr-tauri-m-2606`. ## Documentation The full documentation is at [so3lr.github.io](https://so3lr.github.io/), including: - [Command line](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/cli/) and [settings file](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/settings/) - [Molecular dynamics](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/md/) - [ASE calculator](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/ase/) and [dataset evaluation](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/evaluation/) - [Long-range electrostatics](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/electrostatics/) (Ewald, PME, P3M) - [Enhanced sampling](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/enhanced-sampling/) with PySAGES - [Observables](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/observables/), [gradients and Hessians](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/derivatives/) - [Binding energies](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/binding-energies/) - [Fine-tuning](https://so3lr.github.io/training/finetuning/) and [training from scratch](https://so3lr.github.io/training/from-scratch/) - [API reference](https://so3lr.github.io/reference/api/) and [FAQ](https://so3lr.github.io/reference/faq/) ## Datasets The quantum mechanical datasets used for training and testing SO3LR Tauri are available on Zenodo: [10.5281/zenodo.22920714](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22920714). The data for the legacy SO3LR model are at [10.5281/zenodo.14779793](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14779793). ## Contributing The code and models are still evolving, and your feedback is invaluable. We would appreciate if you [open an issue](https://github.com/general-molecular-simulations/so3lr/issues) for any errors, inconsistencies or feature ideas. See [`DEVELOPERS.md`](./DEVELOPERS.md) for development environments and tests. ## Citation If you use SO3LR, please cite the papers below: ```bibtex @article{kabylda2026so3lr, title = {{SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simulations Covering the Periodic Table}}, author = {Kabylda, Adil and Br{\"{u}}nig, Florian N. and Gallegos, Miguel and Frank, J. Thorben and Moerman, Evgeny and Unke, Oliver T. and Chmiela, Stefan and M{\"{u}}ller, Klaus-Robert and Tkatchenko, Alexandre}, journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2611.06237}, year = {2026}, doi = {10.48550/arXiv.2611.06237}, url = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06237}, } @article{kabylda2025molecular, title={Molecular Simulations with a Pretrained Neural Network and Universal Pairwise Force Fields}, author={Kabylda, Adil and Frank, J Thorben and Su{\'a}rez-Dou, Sergio and Khabibrakhmanov, Almaz and Medrano Sandonas, Leonardo and Unke, Oliver T and Chmiela, Stefan and M{\"u}ller, Klaus-Robert and Tkatchenko, Alexandre}, journal={Journal of the American Chemical Society}, volume={147}, number={37}, pages={33723}, year={2025}, doi={10.1021/jacs.5c09558} } @article{frank2024euclidean, title={A Euclidean transformer for fast and stable machine learned force fields}, author={Frank, Thorben and Unke, Oliver and M{\"u}ller, Klaus-Robert and Chmiela, Stefan}, journal={Nature Communications}, volume={15}, number={1}, pages={6539}, year={2024}, doi={10.1038/s41467-024-50620-6} } ``` ## License The code and the legacy SO3LR model weights are released under the [MIT License](LICENSE), and the SO3LR Tauri weights under [CC BY-NC 4.0](licenses/LICENSE.CC-BY-NC-4.0).
